name: Call of Water
summary: A shaman travels from the Barrens to the Ruins of Stardust for the final gathering trial in the journey to earn Call of Water. Brine sends the initiate north into Ashenvale to draw pure water from its ancient fountain.

sections.title: Journey Into the Twilight Grove
sections.body: After gathering water from the pool below Brine’s hut in the Barrens and the pure well of Tarren Mill, the shaman needs one final essence. Brine sends the initiate north across the dry plains and into Ashenvale, an ancient woodland sacred to the night elves. The dry Barrens give way to Ashenvale’s deep canopy, where water takes another form. A shaman must understand this variety to live in harmony with the element.

sections.title: The Ruins of Stardust
sections.body: Beyond the shimmering waters of Mystral Lake, near the mountain pass between Ashenvale and the Stonetalon Mountains, lie the Ruins of Stardust. An ancient fountain rests among quiet waters and old stones in this secluded elven sanctum. Untamed elemental and nature spirits guard the ruins and resent intruders. The shaman must tread carefully to draw water from the fountain.

sections.title: The Draught of Purest Water
sections.body: Brine receives the filled blue waterskin after the shaman’s pilgrimage across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. She combines the pure fountain water with the samples from the Barrens watering hole and Tarren Mill, then prepares a vial of the purest water. This draught prepares the shaman for the next trial: communion with water elemental spirits through the seer Islen Waterseer.

faq.q: Where are the Ruins of Stardust located?
aliases: how to get to ruins of stardust
faq.answer: The Ruins of Stardust lie in southwestern Ashenvale. From the Barrens, travel north, then follow the roads west past Mystral Lake toward the foothills of the Stonetalon Mountains.

faq.q: Why does Brine need water from an elven ruin?
faq.answer: A shaman gathers water from different expressions of the element to commune with the water spirits. The fountain in the Ruins of Stardust holds ancient, magically pure water untouched by the Barrens’ dry blight, completing the three essences Brine needs for her ritual mixture.

faq.q: What threats exist around the Ruins of Stardust?
faq.answer: Protective beasts and nature spirits guard the ruins and nearby waters. Territorial water elementals and beasts native to Ashenvale attack those who disturb the grove.

faq.q: Who is Brine and why is she helping?
faq.answer: Brine is an ascetic orc shaman who lives in a lone hut in the southern Barrens. As an elder guide assisting Islen Waterseer, she tests prospective shamans’ patience, endurance, and understanding of water before bestowing the element’s blessings.

faq.q: What happens after bringing this water to Brine?
aliases: where do i go after brine
faq.answer: When Brine receives the third sample, she combines the waters to make a draught of the purest water. Then she sends the shaman to Islen Waterseer on the eastern Barrens coast for visionary communion with the elementals.

faq.q: Is Ashenvale safe for low-level Horde shamans?
faq.answer: Ashenvale is contested territory where night elves and the Horde clash. The route through the southern woods avoids major night elf settlements such as Astranaar, but wandering wildlife, aggressive elementals, and Alliance patrols are hazards for an initiate.

angles.text: As a shaman, you cross dangerous borders in search of balance and gather the final fluid essence needed to bind the Water Totem.
As a Horde traveler, you enter ancient Kaldorei lands, where the Warsong Outriders wage an ongoing timber war against hostile night elf sentinels.
As a Tauren, you travel from the arid homelands of central Kalimdor to sacred groves remembered in myth and elder songs.
